feature_flags.name: FEATURE_MEMORY_SHADOW_LOGGING
feature_flags.documented_state: off in code; not yet deployed/observed in any environment
feature_flags.evidence_scope: code default only, per feature_flags.py's registry docstring

notes: Phase 2 scope only: MemoryRetrievalRequest/MemorySnapshot contract + build_memory_snapshot() + a debug-only shadow-comparison helper.
Hard filters (tenant, then entity/session, then domain) applied before any ranking; ranking is deterministic recency only — no embeddings, no vector DB, no LLM-based ranking.

Business Memory (Airtable) carries no tenant_id field today — retrieval only attaches Business Memory content for the single known tenant ('boss_hq') and returns empty (not an error) for any other tenant_id, documented in core/memory_retrieval.py.

Store unavailability (Episodic Postgres down, Business Memory Airtable call failing) is caught per-category and recorded in SnapshotMetadata; only a malformed request (missing tenant_id/canonical_user_id) raises.

No writes to Business Memory/Episodic Memory/context/prompt anywhere in this surface, no calls to the LLM or the approval/tool-execution pipeline — verified by a dedicated test (test_memory_retrieval.py::test_no_llm_or_action_gateway_or_write_calls).

Phase 2B follow-up (2026-08-19): FEATURE_MEMORY_SHADOW_LOGGING (default off) adds a daily scheduler job (scheduler.py::_job_memory_shadow_scan) that writes ONLY structured comparison counts (never memory item text, and error fields are the exception class name only — never the raw exception message) to a new memory_shadow_comparisons Postgres table, so a later Phase 3/cutover decision has owner-scoped scheduled comparison evidence — one sample/day for the single owner identity, not a broad or tenant-wide dataset — see record_shadow_comparison() in core/memory_retrieval_shadow.py and core/migrations/004_memory_shadow_comparisons.sql. This is the one intentional write path in the surface; it writes observability data about the comparison, not to Business Memory/Episodic Memory/context/prompt.
